messages:
Maya: Quick coordination check — we need to bump versions across api, runtime, console, and SDKs for the 0.15 cut. I want to run a staggered merge lane to minimize fallout:
- Slot A (09:00-10:30 PT): api + runtime (minimal breaking changes only)
- Slot B (10:45-11:15 PT): console UI + docs
- Slot C (11:30-12:00 PT): sdk packages and integration tests
Can everyone confirm if those slots work and call out any blockers. Also we need a single changelog PR that compiles the short notes from each repo.

Lee: Slot A works for me. Runtime has one small API signature tweak (model config field optional -> renamed) — I can make it backward-compatible but it means runtime needs a minor version bump and api should accept both keys for one release.

Sam: Noted — I'll add a compatibility shim in api to accept both keys, then deprecate in changelog. ETA for the shim PR is EOD today.

Nina: Console can hold until Slot B. I'll pick up the changelog PR template and add a section for console UI notes. Do we want the changelog to be a single file in the release repo or per-repo and then a top-level aggregator?

Maya: Prefer per-repo release notes (short bullets) submitted as PRs, and then I (release lead) will open the top-level aggregator PR that pulls those snippets. Keeps ownership clear. Nina — can you file a tiny PR with the console notes before 10:00 PT?

Nina: Yep, I'll do that.

Sam: Quick question on SDKs: do we want to bump all language SDKs to mirror the api/runtime minor? Node and Python are ready, go modules have one failing test (timeouts) — I'll most likely land a fix in the morning and then publish. If the fix is delayed, should we still merge SDK changes during Slot C?

Maya: If a language has a failing test that blocks publishing, hold merging until the test is green. We can still merge non-publish changes (docs/README) but mark the publish step as manual. We don't want half-published SDKs.

Lee: For the runtime bump, I'm adding a migration note in the runtime changelog and a compat-test in integration suite. Also opening a canary tag to run on staging GPU pool during Slot A. CI pipeline will run perf smoke tests.

deploy-bot: CI update — integration/all passed for api #4821, runtime #771 (pending perf smoke).

Sam: If perf smoke for runtime fails in canary, what's our fallback plan?

Maya: Fallback: revert runtime PR and keep API shim for a hotfix release. We should also have a queued rollback cut for the staging routing rule. I'll draft the rollback checklist and attach it to the aggregator PR.

Lee: One more ask — can someone from eng-sre reserve the staging GPU pool for Slot A? I don't want other tests contending with canary perf.

Nina: Pinged @eng-sre earlier, will follow up.

Maya: Great. Action items summary:
- Sam: API shim PR (today EOD)
- Lee: Runtime compat + canary tag (Slot A)
- Nina: Console PR + changelog snippet (before 10:00 PT)
- SDK owners: only merge publish-ready packages in Slot C; otherwise merge docs only
- Maya: Create aggregator PR and rollback checklist

Maya: Tagging this with :shipit: when everyone's green. If any blocker appears, drop it here and we'll re-slot.
